signin.summary: Page geometry, the brand lockup, the footer row and the primary-button colour are close, and the card is left-aligned in both (it is NOT centred on this frame). The biggest differences are the heading and body copy, the missing 'Continue with Google' button and 'or' divider (no OAuth exists in the repo), the 'Forgot?' link moved out of the label row, an extra info banner, and the field styling (label ink and size, input well fill, a placeholder that fails AA at 3.45:1). Card-level differences that repeat on every auth state (fields, buttons, card width, banner) are listed once here.

findings.title: Sign-in heading copy
findings.figma: Heading 'Welcome back', Inter Bold 26 text/primary, left-aligned (node 505:124, text at x=541 y=233.5, ta LEFT).
findings.build: Heading 'Sign in to SelahCue' (SignInView.vue:318, .au-title.au-title-form 26px/700). Size, weight and ink match; the words do not. 'Sign in to SelahCue' is the DESKTOP A1 title (ACCOUNT-SETUP-HANDOFF.md:63), not the web frame.
findings.evidence: python3 scripts/vp_style_diff.py --slug signin --dom $RUN/marketing/signin.blink.dom.json --limit 0 -> figma-only 'Welcome back' (y=233.5, 26x700); build-only 'Sign in to SelahCue' (au-title au-title-form, y=197.4). Figma text-align is LEFT, so the heading is not centred.
findings.fix: Change the h1 text in SignInView.vue:318 to 'Welcome back' (keep the h1, tabindex=-1 and the focusHeading behaviour). Update the strings pinned in tests/authViews.test.ts and scripts/auth_pages_headless.py if they assert the old heading.

findings.title: Sign-in body copy names billing and a paid plan
findings.figma: Body 'Sign in to manage your plan, billing and license. You don't need an account to run SelahCue — only to manage a paid plan.' 14.5/22 text/muted, three lines (h=66).
findings.build: 'Manage your plan, license and the devices you have activated.' (SignInView.vue:319). 'billing' and 'paid plan' are not claimed; the 'no account needed' sentence was moved into an info banner (see signin-04).
findings.evidence: Style diff: figma-only y=282.5 (14.5x400) vs build-only 'Manage your plan, license…' (au-body, y=249.9). MARKETING-SITE-HANDOFF.md §8 (line 160) lists 'subscription tiers & billing terms' as Assumed. AUTH-LANDING-PAGES-HANDOFF.md §14: no checkout/plan-change/payment-method frames, 'blocked on the commercial model'. implementation/api: the billing provider webhook is a stub (platform/views.py:421 billing_webhook_not_implemented), so there is no live billing provider.
findings.decision: Owner: Figma promises 'billing' and 'a paid plan'; there is no billing or checkout in the repo and the commercial model (pricing decision D1) is open. Approve a body that keeps Figma's layout (three lines, same sentence order) but ships no billing/paid-plan claim, e.g. 'Sign in to manage your plan and license. You don't need an account to run SelahCue.' — or confirm billing is real. The build currently shows the honest shorter copy.

findings.title: 'Continue with Google' button and 'or' divider
findings.figma: Divider row (505:144: two 1px #2b323d rules + 'or' 13/400 text/muted) and a secondary button 'Continue with Google' (505:148: h44 r12 fill #1e232c, 1px #2b323d border, label 14.5/600 text/primary, 18px #f2b53c ellipse standing in for the Google mark 505:149).
findings.build: Neither is rendered. SignInView.vue header comment records why: DEC-007 chose SelahCue-owned email/password and rejected OIDC; the account GraphQL schema has no social mutation; no config key for a provider exists.
findings.evidence: Style diff: figma-only 'or' (y=601.5) and 'Continue with Google' (y=648.5). DECISION-LOG.md:293 (DEC-007). MARKETING-SITE-HANDOFF.md §8 (line 161) lists 'the OAuth provider(s) on Sign in' as an Assumed placeholder. grep of implementation/api finds OIDC only as a redaction pattern (graphql/redaction.py:19), no provider integration.
findings.decision: Owner/Uma: remove the 'or' divider and the Google button from the Sign in frame (DEC-007: email/password only), or reopen DEC-007 to add a social provider. The build correctly ships neither today. ClickUp 17tnw2b0x3h is NOT the owner of this: it removes unbacked claims the build already shows, whereas this is a feature the build never had.

findings.title: Build-only info banner on Sign in
findings.figma: No banner on the card. The 'you don't need an account to run SelahCue' message is the second sentence of the body paragraph (505:124).
findings.build: AuthBanner kind=info 'You don't need an account to run SelahCue' / 'Signing in manages your plan, license and devices. Live presentation works offline, always.' closes the card (SignInView.vue:369), about 107px of height. No handoff specifies a banner for Sign in: AUTH-LANDING-PAGES-HANDOFF.md §1 carries the never-blank invariant on the new /verify and /reset frames, not on 505:124.
findings.evidence: Style diff build-only: '◆' / 'You don't need an account to run SelahCue' (au-banner-title y=642.4) / 'Signing in manages your plan…' (au-banner-body y=663.6). Slice signin-0.png shows the banner under the button.
findings.decision: Uma: should Sign in carry the reassurance banner (build) or the in-body sentence (Figma)? If the banner stays, draw it in 505:124 and drop the sentence from the body; if not, remove the banner and restore the sentence (subject to signin-02).

findings.title: 'Forgot?' link position and label
findings.figma: 'Forgot?' 13/500 accent/brand sits in the Password LABEL row, right-aligned against the label (505:137, x=851 y=451.5 w=48). MARKETING-PORTAL-GAP-FILL-HANDOFF.md §3d: visible text 'Forgot?', aria-label 'Forgot your password?'.
findings.build: A separate row BELOW the password input, text 'Forgot your password?' 13/400 --sc-primary, right-aligned (SignInView.vue:346-348; auth.css:166-170 .au-inline-link margin -4px 0 4px). The comment at auth.css:163 says 'matching Sign in 505:124' but the frame puts it in the label row.
findings.evidence: Style diff: figma-only 'Forgot?' (y=451.5, 13x500) vs build-only 'Forgot your password?' (y=534.9, 13px). Slice signin-0.png.
findings.fix: Add a label-row slot to FormField (label left, link right) and render the link there with visible text 'Forgot?' (13px/500 --sc-primary) and aria-label='Forgot your password?'. Keep the DOM order input then link (position it with CSS) so the tab order stays Email, Password, Forgot, Sign in (GAP-FILL §3d).

findings.title: Field label size, weight and ink (all auth forms)
findings.figma: Label Inter Medium 13, text/muted #9aa4b2 (maps to --sc-text-secondary), 16px line, 7px gap to the input (AUTH-LANDING-PAGES-HANDOFF.md §2.3; e.g. 505:132).
findings.build: Label 14px/600 --sc-text (#f4f6fb): primary ink where Figma has muted, and larger and heavier. 6px gap (FormField.vue:119-134). Same on verify-v3, verify-v6, reset-r1, reset-r2, reset-r3, reset-r4, reset-r7. MARKETING-PORTAL-GAP-FILL-HANDOFF.md §10a documents 14px SemiBold --sc-text for the generic FormField; AUTH §2.3 (later, written for these frames) is the governing spec for auth cards and Figma agrees with it.
findings.evidence: Style diff 'Email' / 'Password': font-size figma 13px vs build 14.0px; font-weight 500 vs 600; colour figma #9aa4b2 vs build #f4f6fb (no '~', so not the token layer).
findings.fix: Auth variant of FormField (FormField is also used by Contact, SignUp, ForgotPassword, Affiliate and Admin settings, so do not change the generic style): label font 500 13px/16px, color var(--sc-text-secondary), gap 7px. Uma to confirm the generic component keeps §10a.

findings.title: Input well fill, padding and focus/error stroke (all auth forms)
findings.figma: Input 358x44, padding 13/14, radius 10, fill bg/base (AUTH §2.2: 'input well' maps to --sc-inset #0f1116, darker than the card), 1px --sc-border; focus 1.5px accent/brand and error 1.5px accent/live with no halo (747:153, 747:183 sw 1.5).
findings.build: Fill --sc-elevated #1c1f28 (a lighter chip than the card), padding 12/16, painted 45px tall; focus = 1px primary border plus 3px rgba(110,92,240,.25) halo; error = 1px --sc-live (FormField.vue:145-180). GAP-FILL §3a/§10a say --sc-elevated, but AUTH §2.2 maps the input well to --sc-inset and the frames draw it. Same on every state with a field.
findings.evidence: Style diff boxes: 'Frame 505:134 … fill figma #0e1116 vs build #1c1f28'; 'field-input build[542,337,356,45]' vs figma[541,389.5,358,44].
findings.fix: Auth variant: background var(--sc-inset); padding 13px 14px; height 44px; focus and error as a 1.5px stroke in --sc-primary / --sc-live (inset box-shadow so layout does not move) and remove the 3px halo.

findings.title: Placeholder text fails AA
findings.figma: Placeholder 'you@yourchurch.org' 15/400 #9aa4b2 on the #0e1116 well = 7.50:1.
findings.build: Placeholder uses --sc-text-muted #6b7383 on --sc-elevated #1c1f28 = 3.45:1, below the 4.5:1 AA minimum for normal text (FormField.vue:158-160; even on --sc-inset it would be 3.96:1). Same on verify-v3, verify-v6, reset-r4.
findings.evidence: $RUN/report.json contrast_survey: the placeholder address on signin, verify-v3, verify-v4, verify-v6, reset-r4, reset-r5 = 3.45 (required 4.5). Style diff colour: figma #9aa4b2 vs build #6b7383.
findings.fix: Auth cards: .field-input::placeholder { color: var(--sc-text-secondary) } (#a7aebe = 7.40:1 on --sc-elevated, 8.49:1 on --sc-inset).

findings.title: Vertical rhythm between fields (all auth forms)
findings.figma: A field is label 16 + gap 7 + input 44 (plus gap 7 + 17px hint/error when one shows); fields sit 18px apart (card gap 18). E.g. 505:131 h67, next field starts +85px.
findings.build: FormField reserves .field-meta min-height 20px under EVERY field even when empty, adds margin-bottom 16px, and the label line box is 21px: pitch 21+6+45+6+20+16 = 114px vs Figma 85px, about +29px per field (FormField.vue:119-125, 224-230). The verify-v6 card is 475 vs 438 tall.
findings.evidence: verify-v3: Figma input bottom 516.5 to button top 534.5 = 18px; build input 456+45=501 to button 543 = 42px (diff y-shift +25.0 at the button label). Boxes: 'card 505:128 height figma 518 vs build 591.3'.
findings.fix: Auth variant: .form-field { gap: 7px; margin-bottom: 0 }, .field-meta { min-height: 0 } and render the meta row only when a hint or error exists (17px line, 7px above); make the form a flex column with gap 18px.

findings.title: Button heights and the secondary button border (all auth states)
findings.figma: Primary 358x47 radius 12, label 15.5/600 (505:142); secondary 358x44 radius 12, fill --sc-elevated plus a 1px --sc-border (746:181), label 14.5/600.
findings.build: UiButton size-lg padding 16px makes a <button> 51px tall (auth.css:259-267 only sets min-height, which cannot shrink it); link buttons ('Continue to sign in', 'Back to Sign in') are 55.3px and 53.8px because they inherit the page line-height; the secondary variant has no border (UiButton.vue:108-111). Radius 12 and fonts match.
findings.evidence: Boxes: signin 'ui-button variant-primary … build[542,557,356,51]'; verify-v2 'btn-primary 743:148 height figma 47 vs build 55.3'; verify-v5 'btn-secondary 746:181 border figma #2b323d 1px vs build none; height figma 44 vs build 53.8'.
findings.fix: auth.css: .au-btn.ui-button { height: 47px; min-height: 47px; padding-block: 0; line-height: 1.2 }, .au-btn.au-btn-secondary { height: 44px; border: 1px solid var(--sc-border) }. Auth-scoped override, so the shared UiButton does not have to change.

findings.title: Card content is 356px wide, Figma 358px
findings.figma: Card 430 wide, padding 36, 1px stroke drawn INSIDE the frame, so the content column is 358px (x=541 to 899).
findings.build: border-box 430 with a 1px CSS border plus 36px padding leaves 356px (x=542) (auth.css:54-65). Every text box, input and button is 2px narrower. Visible effect: on verify-v1 the title 'Verifying your email address…' is one 29px line in Figma but wraps to two 30px lines in the build (h1 h=60), making that card 33px taller (272 vs 239). Likely cause: the title's natural width is about 357px, between 356 and 358 (not measured directly).
findings.evidence: Boxes: 'input … figma[541,.,358,44] build[542,.,356,45]'; verify-v1 dom h1 h=60 th=59; verify-v1 diff 'card 743:129 height figma 239 vs build 272'; slice verify-v1-0.png.
findings.fix: auth.css:54-65: .au-card { padding: 35px } (35 + 1px border = 36px inset, content 358px) and the mobile paddings 24 to 23 and 20/18 to 19/17. Re-check the V1 title stays on one line.

findings.title: Brand-coloured link text fails AA in the design and in the build
findings.figma: Link text in accent/brand #5b6bd6: footer links ('Create an account', 'Back to Sign in', 'Contact support') 14/600 on #0e1116 = 4.07:1; 'Forgot?' 13/500 on #171b22 = 3.72:1. Both below 4.5:1 for small text.
findings.build: --sc-primary #6e5cf0: footer links 4.12:1 on --sc-base, 'Forgot your password?' 3.83:1 on --sc-surface. The build matches the design intent and so inherits the failure (auth.css:166-186, 280-290).
findings.evidence: $RUN/report.json contrast_survey: 'Create an account', 'Back to Sign in', 'Contact support' 4.12 on signin, verify-v1/v2/v3/v4/v5/v6, reset-r1..r7; 'Forgot your password?' 3.83 on signin. Computed Figma values: 4.07 and 3.72.
findings.decision: Uma: the AA failure is in the Figma colour, so the build cannot fix it by matching. Choose a link ink of at least 4.5:1 on --sc-base and --sc-surface, for example --sc-primary-hover #7e6eff (5.15:1 on --sc-base, 4.79:1 on --sc-surface) or #8a7cff (5.93:1 and 5.51:1), and update the frames.

findings.title: Eye toggle inside the password field
findings.figma: Password field drawn with bullets only, no show/hide control (505:140).
findings.build: FormField draws an eye / eye-off icon button inside the field, a tab stop between Password and Forgot (FormField.vue:81-97, 187-210). Tab order is Email, Password, Show password, Forgot, Sign in, Create an account.
findings.evidence: dom focus list for signin: input, input, button 'Show password', a 'Forgot your password?', button 'Sign in', a 'Create an account'.
findings.source: MARKETING-PORTAL-GAP-FILL-HANDOFF.md §3a ('Filled' row: password shows dots with a show/hide toggle, eye icon) and §10a (password toggle: eye / eye-off icon inside the field). On /reset the later AUTH handoff §5.1/§8.2/§12 specifies the text 'Show' instead: see reset-r1-01.

findings.title: Sign-in states other than the default have no frame
findings.figma: Only the default state is drawn (505:124). MARKETING-PORTAL-GAP-FILL-HANDOFF.md §3b specifies submitting, wrong credentials, rate limited, server error and success in prose; its Figma frames are 'to be added' (GAP-07).
findings.build: The build renders submitting (button spinner, fields 50%), a rejection banner 'Invalid email or password' / 'Check both and try again.' (§3b says 'Please try again.'), 'Too many attempts' / 'Wait a few minutes, then try again.' (§3b specifies a countdown; the API gives no retry-after), an unreachable banner, a session-expired notice 'You've been signed out', 'This account isn't ready to sign in yet' (POLICY_DENIED), a signed-in-but-redirect-failed card, and a resend-sent card. Field errors read 'Enter your email address.' / 'Enter a valid email address.' / 'Enter your password.' where §3c says 'Email is required' / 'Please enter a valid email address' / 'Password is required'. Copy for the last four states is in no handoff. SignInView.vue deliberately has one rejection message (header comment: no account-existence oracle).
findings.evidence: SignInView.vue (state machine and template); lib/auth/messages.ts; lib/auth/emailPolicy.ts:81-82; GAP-FILL §3b, §3c.
findings.decision: Uma: draw frames for these states (or confirm the prose) so the build can be reviewed against a design, and say which validation wording is canonical (GAP-FILL §3c or the shipped emailPolicy wording).

findings.title: No password-length rule on Sign in
findings.figma: GAP-FILL §3c: password 'Too short (<8 chars)' shows 'Password must be at least 8 characters'. Figma draws no validation state.
findings.build: Sign in validates only email format and an empty password ('Enter your password.'); a short password is submitted to the server (SignInView.vue:131-146 validate(), comment inside it).
findings.evidence: SignInView.vue:131-146.
findings.source: AUTH-LANDING-PAGES-HANDOFF.md §11.2: GAP-FILL §3c/§4d password rules are wrong (API is 10-200 characters, length-only). SignInView.vue:131-146 (comment): a length message on a sign-in form would leak policy and lock out legacy passwords.

findings.title: Every auth state keeps the site-default document title
findings.figma: n/a: Figma frames have no document title.
findings.build: doc.title is 'SelahCue — Church presentation, reengineered' on all 14 auth captures; no per-state title ('Sign in', 'Verify your email', 'Choose a new password').
findings.evidence: $RUN/marketing/<slug>.blink.dom.json doc.title for signin, verify-v1..v6, reset-r1..r7.
findings.decision: Uma/Farah: WCAG 2.4.2 expects a title that says what the page is for. No handoff specifies titles; propose 'Sign in — SelahCue', 'Verify your email — SelahCue', 'Choose a new password — SelahCue'.

verify-v1.summary: Copy, glyph, the 6px progress track (about one third full, static under reduced motion) and the footer row match. The build left-aligns the disc, title and body where Figma centres them, and the title wraps onto two lines (card 33px taller) because the card content is 2px narrower (signin-11).

findings.title: Disc, title and body are left-aligned; Figma centres them (V1 and V2 only)
findings.figma: Disc centred (743:130 x=692 in a card spanning 505-935), title and body text-align CENTER (x=541 w=358). Only V1 and V2 are centred: V3-V6 and every /reset frame left-align the disc at x=541, as does Sign in.
findings.build: auth.css:64 .au-card { text-align: left } with no centred modifier, so the disc sits at x=542 and title/body are left (dom: disc x=542, text-align left). Same on verify-v2. The V1 title also wraps (see verify-v1-03).
findings.evidence: python3 scripts/vp_style_diff.py --slug verify-v1 --dom $RUN/marketing/verify-v1.blink.dom.json --limit 0 -> 'text-align figma center vs build left' on the title and body; '↻ x -148.6 px (figma 709.5, build 560.9)'. Slice verify-v1-0.png.
findings.fix: Add a centred modifier (e.g. AuthShell prop align='center' adding .au-card-center) used only by VerifyView states 'verifying' and 'verified': .au-card-center .au-disc { align-self: center }, .au-card-center .au-title, .au-card-center .au-body { text-align: center }. Leave banners, buttons and the footer unchanged (the V2 banner copy stays left at x=583).

findings.title: V1 live region contains no text
findings.figma: AUTH-LANDING-PAGES-HANDOFF.md §4.1 and §12: V1 is announced with role=status aria-live=polite.
findings.build: VerifyView.vue:206-208 puts role=status on a div that wraps only the progress track, with an aria-label and no text node. Assistive tech announces live-region text changes, not an aria-label on insertion, and the h1 is outside the region, so the announcement may be silent.
findings.evidence: VerifyView.vue:206-208; dom: the role=status element has no text.
findings.fix: Put text inside the live region: the body sentence ('This only takes a moment. Keep this tab open.') or an sr-only 'Verifying your email address…'.

findings.title: V1 title wraps to two lines in the build because the web font measures wider than Figma's Inter
findings.figma: V1 (743:125) draws 'Verifying your email address…' on one line in a 358px column, so the card is 239px tall.
findings.build: The title wraps to two lines and the card is 272px (+33px): its natural width in the browser is 360px, wider than both the build's column (356px) and Figma's (358px). Making the column 358px (signin-11) alone will not stop the wrap.
findings.evidence: Measured by QA in Chromium (Quinn Q-2): natural title width 360px; the V1 style diff shows the title as two lines; the Inter cause is inferred, not measured
findings.decision: Uma: allow the V1 title to wrap (and redraw the frame at two lines), or give the title a slightly smaller size or tighter tracking so it fits in 358px. The cause is the web font's metrics against Figma's Inter, not a layout bug, so no engineer fix can make both true.

verify-v2.summary: Content, success disc and banner colours, the primary action and the 'Not your account? Contact support' footer match. Differences are the left alignment (as V1), the banner typography and spacing that every banner in the build shares, and a focus ring the heading shows on arrival.

findings.title: Banner typography, glyph size and spacing (all banners)
findings.figma: Banner 358 wide, padding 14/16, radius 12, 12px between glyph and copy; glyph Inter Bold 15 in the status ink; title Semi Bold 13 text/primary; body Regular 12.5/17 text/muted; 3px title-to-body gap; a three-line body gives 98px (745:124).
findings.build: gap 10px; glyph 13px/700 on a 20px line (it reads as a dot); title 13.5/600; body 13px/19px; title margin-bottom 2px (auth.css:121-159). Same three lines give 107.3px (+9.3). Same on verify-v3, verify-v5, reset-r1, reset-r2, reset-r3, reset-r4, reset-r6, reset-r7: V5 88.3 vs 81, R1 126.3 vs 115, R7 107.3 vs 98.
findings.evidence: python3 scripts/vp_style_diff.py --slug verify-v2 --dom $RUN/marketing/verify-v2.blink.dom.json --limit 0 -> '✓ font-size figma 15px vs build 13.0px'; 'line-height figma 17px vs build 19.0px'; 'banner 745:124 height figma 98 vs build 107.3'; banner text x -3.2 to -7.6 px.
findings.fix: auth.css: .au-banner { gap: 12px }; .au-banner-glyph { font-size: 15px; line-height: 18px }; .au-banner-title { font-size: 13px; line-height: 16px; margin: 0 0 3px }; .au-banner-body { font-size: 12.5px; line-height: 17px }.

findings.title: Typographic apostrophes in Figma copy, ASCII in the build and the copy deck
findings.figma: Figma auth copy uses U+2019: 'You don’t need an account to run SelahCue', 'didn’t', 'we’ll', 'Don’t close this tab.' (Sign in's own copy in Figma uses straight apostrophes).
findings.build: The build renders ASCII ' everywhere (VerifyView.vue, ResetView.vue, lib/auth/messages.ts), as does the handoff copy deck (§8). The pinned test strings (tests/authCopy.test.ts, scripts/auth_pages_headless.py) also use ASCII.
findings.evidence: Style diff 'copy-case' lines on verify-v2, verify-v3, verify-v5, reset-r1..r4, r6, r7.
findings.decision: Uma: which is canonical? Typographic apostrophes are the better typography; adopting them means changing the copy constants and the pinned test strings together.

findings.title: Heading takes programmatic focus and shows a 2px brand outline on arrival
findings.figma: No focus indicator on the title.
findings.build: On arrival at a terminal state focusHeading() moves focus to the h1 (tabindex=-1) and .au-title:focus-visible paints a 2px --sc-primary outline, offset 4px (VerifyView.vue:111-114, 378-381). It shows in the verify-v2 and verify-v3 captures; the h1 is not a tab stop.
findings.evidence: Slice verify-v2-0.png (outline around 'Email address verified'); dom focus list has no h1.
findings.source: AUTH-LANDING-PAGES-HANDOFF.md §12 (focus order brand then card title; 2px accent/brand ring with offset); implementation/marketing/scripts/auth_pages_headless.py:1289 pins 'V2 focus moved to the heading'; VerifyView.vue:102-110 explains why.

verify-v3.summary: This is the state that ships and its structure, copy, disc, resend form and banner all match; the card reads 46px taller than Figma. Every difference is one of the card-level ones listed under signin, verify-v2 and reset-r2.

findings.title: Card is 46px taller than Figma (acceptance numbers for this state)
findings.figma: Card 746:128 is 430x554: disc 56, two-line title 58, three-line body 66, one field 67, button 47, banner 98, all 18px apart.
findings.build: Card is 430x600.3: field block +29 (label line box, reserved meta row, margin-bottom), button +4, banner +9.3, title lines +2 (about +44 of the +46). Disc, title wrap, body lines and banner lines all match.
findings.evidence: python3 scripts/vp_style_diff.py --slug verify-v3 --dom $RUN/marketing/verify-v3.blink.dom.json --limit 0 -> 'card 746:128 height figma 554 vs build 600.3'; 'input … build[542,456,356,45]'; 'btn-primary … build 51'; 'banner 746:140 height figma 98 vs build 107.3'.
findings.fix: No separate change: closes when signin-06, signin-07, signin-09, signin-10, signin-11 and verify-v2-01 land. Acceptance: at 1440x900 the card is 554px tall, the input top sits 23px below the label top, the button is 47px, the banner 98px.

findings.title: Transport-failure state and resend errors have no frame
findings.figma: /verify has no server-error frame (/reset has R7). The resend form has no pending or error frame.
findings.build: VerifyView.vue:332-348 renders a warning disc '!', 'We couldn't verify your email just now', 'We couldn't reach SelahCue. Check your connection and try again — this page is the only thing affected.', primary 'Try again' and a success banner 'Your link still works', extrapolated from R7 (comment at :326-331). Resend failures show a role=alert note (RESEND_FAILED / RESEND_RATE_LIMITED, lib/auth/messages.ts).
findings.evidence: VerifyView.vue:326-348; scripts/auth_pages_headless.py scenario 'verify-unreachable'.
findings.decision: Uma: draw the V-series transport-failure state and the resend pending/error states, or confirm the R7-derived layout and copy.

verify-v4.summary: V4 ('This verification link has expired', 24-hour TTL) is deliberately not rendered: the API cannot tell an expired token from an invalid one, so the build ships the merged V3 for every token failure. The verify-v4 capture is the V3 card, the shipped substitute.

findings.title: V4 'link expired' is designed but not rendered; V3 ships for every failure
findings.figma: Warn disc '!' #f2b53c, title 'This verification link has expired', body 'Verification links expire 24 hours after they are sent…', Email field + 'Send a new verification link', warn banner 'Why links expire', footer 'Wrong address? Back to Sign in' (746:148).
findings.build: Not rendered. VerifyView.vue state 'invalid' (V3) covers every token failure with copy that names expiry, reuse and a bad copy without asserting which (VerifyView.vue:8-23, 230-266). The verify-v4 capture is scenario 'verify-invalid' (dom h1 = V3 title).
findings.evidence: surfaces.json: status not-rendered with source_probe must_not_contain 'This verification link has expired'. Style diff: 7 figma-only texts ('!', title, body, banner title/body/glyph, 'Wrong address?') vs the V3 equivalents. The 24-hour TTL itself is real (implementation/api/selahcue_api/settings.py:371 ACCOUNT_EMAIL_VERIFY_TTL_SECONDS default 24*3600), so V4 becomes buildable the day the API returns a distinguishable expiry.
findings.source: AUTH-LANDING-PAGES-HANDOFF.md §4.4 ('Only render this when the backend can prove expiry') and §10.2 (verify_email collapses unknown/consumed/expired into one VALIDATION_FAILED; owner decision product + security). ClickUp 86ak120fz is named in VerifyView.vue:22 as the owner of any change.

verify-v5.summary: Reachable only through the resend form (the capture drives it). Copy, conditional no-enumeration wording, secondary 'Back to Sign in', banner and 'Need a hand? Contact support' footer match. The spam-folder note fails AA, and the envelope glyph renders half the drawn size.

findings.title: Helper note ('Didn't arrive?') fails AA
findings.figma: Note 12.5/400, 17px line, text/muted #9aa4b2 on #171b22 = 6.85:1 (746:172 text at y=523.5).
findings.build: au-note is 13px/20px --sc-text-muted #6b7383 on --sc-surface #14161d = 3.79:1, below 4.5:1 (auth.css:106-111). The same class carries R3's 'Don't close this tab.' (reset-r3) and every resend-error note.
findings.evidence: $RUN/report.json contrast_survey verify-v5 "Didn't arrive? Check your spam folder…" 3.79; reset-r3 "Don't close this tab." 3.79. Style diff 'colour figma #9aa4b2 vs build #6b7383' and 'line-height figma 17px vs build 20.0px'.
findings.fix: auth.css .au-note: color var(--sc-text-secondary) (8.12:1 on --sc-surface), font-size 12.5px, line-height 17px.

findings.title: Envelope glyph renders at about 13px, drawn at 22px
findings.figma: '✉︎' (U+2709 + U+FE0E text variation selector) Inter Bold 22 in accent/brand, 22px wide (746:172 text x=558 w=22).
findings.build: StatusDisc glyph '✉' without the selector (VerifyView.vue:303, ResetView.vue:415, SignInView.vue:432); it falls back to a symbol font and measures 13.3px wide at 22px, visibly smaller than the ✓ and ✕ discs (19.8px and 16.8px).
findings.evidence: dom verify-v5 au-disc text '✉' tw 13.3; slice verify-v5-0.png (build envelope is a small purple mark, Figma's is a full-size envelope).
findings.fix: Use '✉︎' (U+2709 U+FE0E) in all three views and check the glyph width is about 22px; if the fallback font still renders it small, pin a font-family that has the glyph.

verify-v6.summary: Copy, the muted (not red) '!' disc, the email form and the 'Already verified? Back to Sign in' footer all match. Only the card-level differences remain; the card reads 37px taller than Figma.

findings.title: Card is 37px taller than Figma (acceptance numbers for this state)
findings.figma: Card 747:128 is 430x438: disc 56, two-line title 58, three-line body 66, one field 67, button 47, all 18px apart; no banner.
findings.build: Card is 430x475: field block +29, button +4, title lines +2. Title and body wrap exactly as Figma. The neutral disc ink is --sc-text-secondary #a7aebe, the mapped text/muted.
findings.evidence: python3 scripts/vp_style_diff.py --slug verify-v6 --dom $RUN/marketing/verify-v6.blink.dom.json --limit 0 -> 'card 747:128 height figma 438 vs build 475'; 'input … build[542,519,356,45]'; 'btn-primary … build 51'.
findings.fix: No separate change: closes when signin-06, signin-07, signin-09, signin-10 and signin-11 land. Acceptance: card 438px tall at 1440x900.

reset-r1.summary: Title, body, both field labels, the hint, 'Update password', the 'This signs you out everywhere' banner and the footer match in copy. The build shows an eye icon where Figma has the text 'Show', does not focus the New password field on arrival, and its hint fails AA at 3.79:1.

findings.title: Password reveal control is an icon, Figma draws the text 'Show' (R1, R2, R3, R7)
findings.figma: Trailing text 'Show' 12.5/500 text/muted inside both inputs (x=851, y=362.5 and 471.5). AUTH-LANDING-PAGES-HANDOFF.md §5.1 'both with a Show affordance', §8.2 trailing 'Show', §12 'Show toggles need aria-pressed and a label that is not just an icon'.
findings.build: A 20px eye / eye-off SVG in a 28x28 button (FormField.vue:81-97, 187-210). aria-label 'Show password'/'Hide password' and aria-pressed are present, but the visible control is only an icon and the desktop hit area is 28px (handoff §12: targets of at least 44px).
findings.evidence: python3 scripts/vp_style_diff.py --slug reset-r1 --dom $RUN/marketing/reset-r1.blink.dom.json --limit 0 -> figma-only 'Show' (y=362.5) and 'Show' (y=471.5); dom password-toggle w=28 h=28.
findings.fix: On /reset render the visible text 'Show' / 'Hide' (12.5px/500 --sc-text-secondary) in the toggle, keep aria-pressed and the aria-label, and give it a 44px-tall hit area. Keep the eye icon on /signin (signin-13).

findings.title: New password is not focused on arrival
findings.figma: R1 draws the New password input focused: 1.5px accent/brand stroke (747:153 s #5b6bd6 sw 1.5); handoff §5.1 '(focused …)'.
findings.build: No field is focused on arrival: ResetView.vue onMounted only sets the state, and the capture shows no focus stroke.
findings.evidence: Slice reset-r1-0.png (no brand stroke on the build's first field); ResetView.vue:217-225.
findings.fix: When a token is present, focus the New password input after mount (nextTick). The h1 stays first in the DOM so screen readers still read the title.

findings.title: Field hint fails AA
findings.figma: Hint 'At least 10 characters.' 12.5/400, 17px line, text/muted #9aa4b2 on #171b22 = 6.85:1 (747:143 text y=399).
findings.build: FormField .field-hint is 13px/19.5px --sc-text-muted #6b7383 on --sc-surface = 3.79:1 (FormField.vue:247-250). Same on reset-r3 and reset-r7.
findings.evidence: $RUN/report.json contrast_survey reset-r1, reset-r3, reset-r7 'At least 10 characters.' 3.79. Style diff 'colour figma #9aa4b2 vs build #6b7383', 'line-height figma 17px vs build 19.5px'.
findings.fix: Auth variant: .field-hint { color: var(--sc-text-secondary); font-size: 12.5px; line-height: 17px }.

reset-r2.summary: Both messages match word for word and both fields turn red, but the message format differs, the submit button is not dimmed, and the build keeps the 'signs you out everywhere' banner that Figma drops, making the card 162px taller.

findings.title: Field error format: icon instead of the text '✕ '
findings.figma: Messages '✕ Password must be at least 10 characters.' and '✕ Both passwords must match.' 12.5/500, 17px line, accent/live, flush with the field edge (x=541). AUTH §12: 'Field errors carry ✕ in the message text itself'.
findings.build: A 14px circle-exclamation SVG plus the message, 13/500 on a 19.5px line, text starting at x=560 (FormField.vue:100-106, 232-245); there is no ✕ character.
findings.evidence: python3 scripts/vp_style_diff.py --slug reset-r2 --dom $RUN/marketing/reset-r2.blink.dom.json --limit 0 -> 'copy figma ✕ Password … vs build Password …', 'x +19.0 px', 'line-height figma 17px vs build 19.5px'.
findings.fix: Auth variant: drop the SVG and prefix '✕ ' to the message (an aria-hidden glyph span is fine, the message keeps role=alert); 12.5px/500, 17px line.

findings.title: Submit button is not dimmed while errors show
findings.figma: 'Update password' at 45% opacity while both fields are in error (747:194; handoff §5.2).
findings.build: Full-strength button (hover fill in the capture), enabled (ResetView.vue:292-301).
findings.evidence: Style diff boxes: 'btn-primary 747:194 fill figma #5b6bd6 vs build #7e6eff'; slice reset-r2-0.png.
findings.fix: While field errors are present set the button to 45% opacity (aria-disabled, still focusable; submitting re-validates) and clear it when either field changes.

findings.title: Info banner kept on R2 and R3; Figma drops it
findings.figma: R2 and R3 end with the button and the footer row; the 'This signs you out everywhere' banner appears on R1 only (747:173, 749:124).
findings.build: ResetView.vue:314 shows the banner in every form state except R7/PASSWORD_INVALID (v-if="!showsErrorBanner"). R2 card is 609.8px tall vs 448; R3 is 647.8 vs 435.
findings.evidence: Style diff build-only on reset-r2 and reset-r3: '◆', 'This signs you out everywhere', 'Updating your password ends every active…'. Boxes: 'card 747:177 height figma 448 vs build 609.8'.
findings.fix: Hide the banner while field errors show (R2) and while submitting (R3). If Uma says the frames abbreviated, close this item.

findings.title: Primary button hover fill fails AA with the white label
findings.figma: No hover frame. Rest state: white label on accent/brand #5b6bd6 = 4.65:1.
findings.build: UiButton .variant-primary:hover uses --sc-primary-hover #7e6eff under a white 15.5/600 label = 3.78:1 (UiButton.vue:104-106). The scripted click leaves the pointer on the button, so the R2, R3 and R4 captures show the hover fill (dom button bg rgb(126,110,255)). Rest fill #6e5cf0 is 4.72:1 and passes.
findings.evidence: $RUN/report.json contrast_survey: reset-r2 'Update password', reset-r3 'Updating password…', reset-r4 'Send a new reset link' value 3.78 (required 4.5).
findings.fix: Make the hover fill darker than --sc-primary instead of lighter, e.g. #5f4de6 (white 5.69:1), for every primary UiButton, so the label holds 4.5:1 on hover. Uma may choose the exact hover colour under shared-chrome-31; whichever is chosen must measure at least 4.5:1 with the white label. This is a shipped accessibility failure, so it is class A here and the open choice of colour is the class D finding.

reset-r3.summary: aria-busy on the form, the disabled fields and button, and the polite 'Don't close this tab.' status are all in place. But the button hides its 'Updating password…' label behind a generic spinner, the fields are dimmed twice, and the hint and banner Figma omits are still shown.

findings.title: Submitting button hides its 'Updating password…' label
findings.figma: Disabled button at 50% opacity showing '↻' (14/700 white) and 'Updating password…' (15.5/600 white) centred (749:143; texts at x=629.5 and x=651.5). Copy deck §8.2: bold 'Updating password…'.
findings.build: UiButton loading=true sets .content.hidden { opacity: 0 } and shows a 20px generic spinner only (UiButton.vue:48-51, 149-161); the button stays at full strength. The designed '↻' class .au-spinner (auth.css:324-345, static under reduced motion) is defined but used nowhere. The same happens on Sign in ('Signing in…', SignInView.vue:357) and the resend buttons.
findings.evidence: dom: button class 'is-loading', child span.content.hidden opacity 0 text 'Updating password…'; style diff figma-only '↻' and 'Updating password… x -11.8'; slice reset-r3-0.png (build shows a lone spinner).
findings.fix: For auth buttons keep the label visible while loading: .au-btn.is-loading .content { opacity: 1 }, hide .spinner, prefix the label with ↻ (static under prefers-reduced-motion already), and set the button to 50% opacity. Apply to Sign in and the resend buttons too.

findings.title: Fields are dimmed twice and the toggles stay live
findings.figma: Only the two input frames are at 50% (749:134, 749:140); labels stay full strength; the hint is absent.
findings.build: ResetView.vue:467-469 sets .form-field { opacity: .5 } and FormField.vue:182-185 sets .is-disabled .field-input { opacity: .5 }, so inputs sit at 25% and labels at 50%; the hint 'At least 10 characters.' is still drawn; the two 'Show password' buttons remain enabled tab stops (dom focus list: button, button, Back to Sign in).
findings.evidence: dom reset-r3: input opacity '0.5' inside a .form-field at 0.5; style diff build-only 'At least 10 characters.'; slice reset-r3-0.png (labels and inputs visibly faint).
findings.fix: Dim only the input (and its toggle) to 50%, once; leave labels at full strength; hide the hint while submitting; set disabled on the toggle buttons.

reset-r4.summary: This is the state that ships and its copy (including the 1-hour, single-use sentence), the danger disc, the resend form, the 'Your password has not changed' banner and the footer all match. The card reads 45px taller than Figma, from the shared field, button and banner differences.

findings.title: Card is 45px taller than Figma (acceptance numbers for this state)
findings.figma: Card 749:154 is 430x547: disc 56, one-line title 29, four-line body 88, one field 67, button 47, banner 98, all 18px apart.
findings.build: Card is 430x592.3: field block +29, button +4, banner +9.3, title line +1. Body wraps to four lines in both.
findings.evidence: python3 scripts/vp_style_diff.py --slug reset-r4 --dom $RUN/marketing/reset-r4.blink.dom.json --limit 0 -> 'card 749:154 height figma 547 vs build 592.3'; 'input … build[542,452,356,45]'; 'banner 749:166 height figma 98 vs build 107.3'.
findings.fix: No separate change: closes when signin-06, signin-07, signin-09, signin-10, signin-11 and verify-v2-01 land. Acceptance: card 547px tall at 1440x900.

findings.title: /reset 'no link' and 'link sent' states have no frame
findings.figma: The R-series has no frame for opening /reset without ?token= or for the 'new link requested' confirmation; /verify has V6 and V5.
findings.build: ResetView.vue:382-435 renders 'This page needs a reset link' (neutral disc, 'Send a reset link' form) and 'Check your inbox' ('If … has a SelahCue account, a new reset link is on its way. It expires in 1 hour.'), both extrapolated from V6 and V5.
findings.evidence: ResetView.vue:98-101 (state comments), :378-435; scripts/auth_pages_headless.py reset scenarios.
findings.decision: Uma: draw R-series equivalents of V6 and V5, or confirm that the V6/V5 frames are reused with the 1-hour copy.

reset-r5.summary: R5 ('This reset link has expired', 1-hour TTL) is deliberately not rendered: the API cannot tell an expired reset token from an invalid one, so R4 ships for every token failure. The reset-r5 capture is the R4 card, the shipped substitute.

findings.title: R5 'link expired' is designed but not rendered; R4 ships for every failure
findings.figma: Warn disc '!' #f2b53c, title 'This reset link has expired', body contrasting the 1-hour and 24-hour TTLs, Email field + 'Send a new reset link', warn banner 'Why only 1 hour', footer 'Remembered it? Back to Sign in' (749:174).
findings.build: Not rendered. ResetView.vue state 'invalid' (R4) covers every VALIDATION_FAILED and names the 1-hour single-use rule without asserting a cause (ResetView.vue:48-58, 322-357). The reset-r5 capture is scenario 'reset-invalid' (dom h1 = R4 title).
findings.evidence: surfaces.json: status not-rendered with source_probe must_not_contain 'This reset link has expired'. Style diff: 6 figma-only texts ('!', title, body, banner x3) vs the R4 equivalents. The 1-hour TTL is real (implementation/api/selahcue_api/settings.py:372 ACCOUNT_PASSWORD_RESET_TTL_SECONDS default 3600).
findings.source: AUTH-LANDING-PAGES-HANDOFF.md §5.5 ('Needs §10.2 to be reachable') and §10.2 (confirm_password_reset collapses unknown/consumed/expired into one VALIDATION_FAILED; owner decision product + security). ClickUp 86ak120fz is named in ResetView.vue:53 as the owner of any change.

reset-r6.summary: Copy, success disc, 'Continue to sign in', the 'Your devices keep presenting' banner and the 'Didn't do this? Contact support' footer match. Only the shared button-height and banner differences remain; the card reads 20px taller than Figma.

findings.title: Card is 20px taller than Figma (acceptance numbers for this state)
findings.figma: Card 749:202 is 430x440: disc 56, title 29, three-line body 66, button 47, banner 98, all 18px apart.
findings.build: Card is 430x460.5: the link-button 'Continue to sign in' is 55.3px (+8.3), banner +9.3, title line +1 (about +19 of the +20). Disc, copy and wrapping match.
findings.evidence: python3 scripts/vp_style_diff.py --slug reset-r6 --dom $RUN/marketing/reset-r6.blink.dom.json --limit 0 -> 'card 749:202 height figma 440 vs build 460.5'; 'btn-primary 749:207 height figma 47 vs build 55.3'; 'banner 749:209 height figma 98 vs build 107.3'.
findings.fix: No separate change: closes when signin-10 and verify-v2-01 land. Acceptance: card 440px tall at 1440x900.

reset-r7.summary: Danger banner above the title, form, 'Try again' and the reassurance copy match. The footer offers 'Back to Sign in' where Figma offers 'Request a new reset link', and the build also has a PASSWORD_INVALID state no frame covers.

findings.title: Footer link offers sign-in instead of a new reset link
findings.figma: 'Still stuck?' + 'Request a new reset link' 14/600 accent/brand (749:244). Handoff §5.7 'footer offers a fresh link'; copy deck §8.2 R7.
findings.build: 'Still stuck?' + 'Back to Sign in' linking to /signin (ResetView.vue:443). On a state whose banner says the link still works, the way out offered is the wrong page.
findings.evidence: python3 scripts/vp_style_diff.py --slug reset-r7 --dom $RUN/marketing/reset-r7.blink.dom.json --limit 0 -> figma-only 'Request a new reset link' (y=754.5); build-only 'Back to Sign in'; 'Still stuck? x +32.8 px'.
findings.fix: Change the R7 footer link (ResetView.vue:443) to the text 'Request a new reset link' pointing at /forgot-password (route exists, router/index.ts:36).

findings.title: PASSWORD_INVALID state has no frame
findings.figma: R7 is the only form-with-danger-banner frame ('We couldn't update your password').
findings.build: ResetView.vue:252-260 renders the same layout with 'That password wasn't accepted' / 'Your password has not been changed and this reset link still works. Choose a different password and try again.' for a server-side PASSWORD_INVALID. DEC-017 sanctioned the distinct code after the R-series was drawn.
findings.evidence: ResetView.vue:92-97, 248-260; DECISION-LOG.md:36 (DEC-017).
findings.decision: Uma: draw the 'password not accepted' variant of R7 and confirm its copy.
